problem: AI agents typically operate autonomously without human input, but many real-world tasks require human-agent collaboration due to human expertise, preferences, or control requirements.
approach: Collaborative Gym (Co-Gym) provides an open framework with bidirectional communication between agents and humans, enabling non-turn-taking interaction and assessment of both collaboration outcomes and processes.
contribution: Framework demonstrates that collaborative agents outperform autonomous counterparts by 86% win rate in Travel Planning, 74% in Tabular Analysis, and 66% in Related Work when evaluated by real users.

problem: Vision-based reinforcement learning struggles with object-centric representations that fail under occlusions, 3D ambiguity, and entanglement between object configurations and camera poses.
approach: Proposes 3D-aware object-centric representation using multi-view 3D features, explicit 3D-aware disentanglement with multi-view Transformer and prototypical learning, plus a block transformer policy for novel task composition.
contribution: The 3D-aware representation stably identifies 3D object positions and properties with strong interpretability, enabling zero-shot generalization to novel tasks and unseen viewpoints.

problem: Imposing stylistic constraints on LLM outputs via representation editing degrades truthfulness by contaminating the model's core truthfulness representations, creating a trade-off between style and accuracy.
approach: StyliTruth uses orthogonal deflation to separate style-relevant and truth-relevant subspaces in representation space, enabling independent token-level steering vectors for dynamic control of both dimensions.
contribution: Significantly reduces stylization-induced truthfulness collapse and outperforms existing inference-time intervention methods in balancing style adherence with truthfulness across multiple styles and languages.

problem: Electrostatic field matching (EFM) requires complex neural network modeling of fields outside capacitor plates, creating implementation difficulties for data generation and transfer.
approach: Interaction Field Matching (IFM) generalizes EFM to arbitrary interaction fields inspired by strong interactions in physics, solving modeling complexity by using a particular interaction field realization.
contribution: Demonstrates improved performance on toy and image data transfer problems by extending beyond restrictive electrostatic model assumptions.

problem: Deep neural networks remain overconfident on out-of-distribution (OoD) inputs, failing to reliably detect when they encounter data outside their training distribution.
approach: Uses Riemannian information geometry to model predictions as a statistical manifold, quantifying OoD detection via Fisher Information Matrix trace as a measure of local sensitivity.
contribution: Provides theoretical geometric connection between feature magnitude and output uncertainty, creating a unifying framework for OoD detection with competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Discrete video generation methods lag behind continuous approaches due to error accumulation and long-context inconsistency in extended sequences.
approach: URSA formulates video generation as iterative global refinement of discrete spatiotemporal tokens using a Linearized Metric Path and Resolution-dependent Timestep Shifting, with asynchronous temporal fine-tuning.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing discrete methods and matches state-of-the-art continuous approaches while requiring significantly fewer inference steps for high-resolution and long-duration video generation.

problem: Safety alignment of LLMs under reinforcement learning often causes catastrophic forgetting of general abilities, known as the alignment tax, reducing performance on general tasks.
approach: Null-Space constrained Policy Optimization (NSPO) geometrically projects safety policy gradients into the null space of general task gradients, preserving core capabilities while enforcing safety.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art safety performance without sacrificing accuracy on math, code, and instruction-following tasks, using only 40% of standard safety data while outperforming existing methods by a large margin.

problem: Multivariate time series forecasting is challenged by non-stationarity, inter-variable dependencies, and distribution shifts, while existing generative models ignore informative priors like conditional means and covariances.
approach: Conditionally Whitened Generative Models (CW-Gen) incorporates prior information through conditional whitening, using a Joint Mean-Covariance Estimator (JMCE) to learn conditional statistics for diffusion and flow matching models.
contribution: CW-Gen consistently enhances predictive performance on five real-world datasets across six generative models, effectively capturing non-stationary dynamics and mitigating distribution shift effects.

problem: Current language agents employ uniform chain-of-thought reasoning across all scenarios, resulting in excessive token usage and inflexible social behaviors in dynamic social interactions like negotiation.
approach: Adaptive Social Learning (ASL) framework identifies hierarchical reasoning modes from intuitive to deep deliberation, using Adaptive Mode Policy Optimization (AMPO) to learn context-aware mode switching.
contribution: ASL achieves 15.6% higher task performance than GPT-4o with 32.8% shorter thinking chains by adapting reasoning depth to context, outperforming GRPO on token efficiency and reasoning quality.

problem: Continual learning with frozen large pre-trained models faces the stability-plasticity dilemma as shallow adaptation modules struggle between preserving prior knowledge and learning new information.
approach: MaRS (Memory-Adaptive Router with Statistical control) decouples stable representation from adaptive capacity using a frozen encoder, slot-based memory router, and lightweight classifier with statistical expansion guarantees.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance with frozen LPMs through controlled slot expansion and dual-stage contrastive-distillation adaptation that preserves prior knowledge without raw replay.

problem: Tropical tree crown detection in high-resolution drone imagery is hindered by wide variation in crown size, structure, and pattern, along with severe overlapping and intertwining of crowns.
approach: SelvaBox dataset provides 83,000 manually labeled tropical tree crowns from three countries in high-resolution imagery, benchmarked across multi-resolution unified pipeline approaches.
contribution: Dataset achieves competitive zero-shot detection on unseen tropical datasets, and jointly training on SelvaBox with other datasets yields a detector ranking first or second across all evaluated datasets.

problem: Large-scale knowledge editing on LLMs while maintaining Reliability, Generality, and Locality metrics remains a significant challenge requiring efficient, low-cost modification methods.
approach: Massive editing approach (MeG) attaches a dynamic weight neuron to specific LLM layers and uses a diffusion model to conditionally generate neuron weights based on input queries.
contribution: MeG significantly improves performance on Reliability, Generality, and Locality metrics compared to existing knowledge editing methods, with particularly large gains on Locality index.

problem: Current vision-language navigation methods produce fragmented motions, high latency, and struggle with real-world challenges like dynamic obstacle avoidance through end-to-end action mappings.
approach: DualVLN combines System 2 (VLM-based global planner predicting waypoints via image-grounded reasoning) with System 1 (lightweight Diffusion Transformer policy for smooth trajectory generation).
contribution: Outperforms prior methods on all VLN benchmarks and demonstrates robust real-time control with adaptive local decision-making in complex, dynamic environments in real-world experiments.

problem: Image forgery localization faces new challenges in the generative AI era as diffusion-based editing creates photorealistic, semantically coherent manipulations that evade conventional detectors.
approach: Detective SAM builds on SAM2 foundation model, integrating perturbation-driven forensic clues with feature and mask adapters to convert clues into forgery masks via automatic prompting.
contribution: Delivers 33.67% relative IoU gain over best baseline (36.99 IoU / 44.19 F1) with stable out-of-distribution performance and quick adaptation to new editors via AutoEditForge synthetic data pipeline.

problem: Cross-view completion (CroCo) is effective for geometric tasks but its photometric understanding capabilities remain underexplored for relighting and illumination-related tasks.
approach: Disentangles CroCo latent representations into a single illumination vector and patch-wise intrinsic vectors using self-supervised cross-lighting and intrinsic consistency losses on paired images under different illumination.
contribution: Demonstrates that the lighting latent can be manipulated for interpolation between lighting conditions, shadow removal, and albedo estimation, showing feasibility of CroCo for photometric downstream tasks.

problem: Deploying domain-specific embedding models in resource-constrained environments is challenging due to their large parameter counts, and existing pruning methods fail to distinguish domain-specific from general patterns.
approach: GAPrune uses Fisher Information for importance measurement and general-domain gradient alignment assessment, combining signals via Domain Alignment Importance (DAI) scoring to guide pruning decisions.
contribution: Maintains within 2.5% of dense model performance at 50% sparsity with one-shot pruning and improves 4.51% on FinMTEB and 1.73% on ChemTEB with 100 retraining steps.

problem: Comparing bias mitigation methods is difficult due to heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent fairness metrics, and isolated evaluation of vision models versus LVLMs without fair hyperparameter tuning.
approach: NH-Fair provides a unified benchmark spanning vision and LVLMs under standardized data, metrics, and training protocols, with systematic ERM tuning study to identify high-impact training choices.
contribution: Shows that many debiasing methods don't reliably outperform well-tuned ERM baseline, while composite data-augmentation consistently delivers parity gains without sacrificing utility.

problem: Existing caching methods for Flow Matching inference reduce computation but rely on instantaneous velocity leading to severe trajectory deviations and error accumulation under high acceleration ratios.
approach: MeanCache leverages cached Jacobian-vector products to construct interval average velocities, with a trajectory-stability scheduling strategy using Peak-Suppressed Shortest Path under budget constraints.
contribution: Achieves 4.12x on FLUX.1, 4.56x on Qwen-Image, and 3.59x on HunyuanVideo acceleration while outperforming caching baselines in generation quality.

problem: Combining LoRA with mixture-of-experts for multi-task LLM adaptation often replaces entire layers with experts or appends parallel branches, undermining parameter efficiency and task specialization.
approach: LoRA-Mixer routes task-specific LoRA experts into attention module projection matrices via a Routing Specialization Loss (RSL) that enforces load balance and input-aware specialization.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on 15 benchmarks including MedQA, GSM8K, and HumanEval using 48% fewer trainable parameters, with gains of 3.79% on GSM8K and 3.95% on ARC-C.

problem: Two-handed fingerspelling detection and recognition is rarely evaluated in existing sign language datasets, particularly for BANZSL which requires handling handshape coarticulation and self-occlusion.
approach: BANZ-FS dataset includes 35,000+ fingerspelling instances from news broadcasts, laboratory recordings, and social media with multi-level video-subtitle-letter-lexicon alignment annotations.
contribution: Highlights unique linguistic and visual challenges of two-handed fingerspelling while benchmarking detection, isolated recognition, and recognition-in-context tasks on the largest BANZSL dataset.

problem: The assumption that reasoning capabilities only emerge in large models trained on massive datasets remains largely unquestioned, despite sub-billion parameter models showing promise.
approach: Carefully curates and resamples open-source datasets under designed metrics, showing that high-quality data (~2T tokens) combined with pre-training (4.2T) enables strong sub-billion reasoning models.
contribution: X-LLM-R1-950M achieves 15.5 AIME score on only 11.7% of Qwen3's token budget, matching or surpassing Qwen3-0.6B while trained entirely on open-sourced data.

problem: Active Deep Probabilistic Subsampling (A-DPS) does not fully leverage valuable dataset priors and relies on top-1 sampling which can impede the optimization process in subsampling tasks.
approach: Prior-aware and context-guided Group-based Active DPS (PGA-DPS) integrates deterministic prior-informed sampling patterns with group-based top-k sampling to achieve robust optimization.
contribution: Outperforms A-DPS, DPS, and all other sampling methods on classification, image reconstruction, and segmentation tasks across MNIST, CIFAR-10, fastMRI, and AeroRIT datasets.

problem: A significant gap remains between prover LLMs solving substantially fewer problems than general-purpose LLMs in natural language due to the complexity of formal theorem proving.
approach: Hilbert is an agentic framework combining informal LLM reasoning with Lean 4 prover, using recursive decomposition, formal verification, and semantic theorem retrieval to bridge reasoning and proving.
contribution: Achieves 99.2% on miniF2F (6.6 points above best public method) and 70.0% on PutnamBench (422% improvement over best public baseline), demonstrating best known results.

problem: Object detection quantization preserves redundant activations from cluttered backgrounds and irregular morphologies, wasting bit capacity and failing to preserve informative features.
approach: InlierQ computes gradient-aware volume saliency scores, classifies volumes as inliers/outliers via EM algorithm, and suppresses outlier influence while preserving informative inlier features.
contribution: Achieves consistent quantization error reductions across camera-based 2D/3D and LiDAR-based 3D object detection on COCO and nuScenes benchmarks as a label-free, drop-in method.

problem: Speech Language Models transitioning to shared multi-user environments must distinguish between users to prevent unauthorized information disclosure, a capability absent in current models.
approach: VoxPrivacy benchmark evaluates interactional privacy across three difficulty tiers from direct secrecy commands to proactive privacy protection on a 32-hour bilingual dataset.
contribution: Reveals widespread vulnerability where most open-source models perform near random chance (50% accuracy) on conditional privacy decisions, while even strong closed-source systems fail on proactive inference.

problem: Embodied agents in partially observable multi-agent environments must plan despite uncertainty about hidden objects and intentions, typically requiring heavy inter-agent communication.
approach: Planner-Composer-Evaluator (PCE) framework converts LLM reasoning assumptions into a structured decision tree with scenario likelihood, goal-directed gain, and execution cost scoring.
contribution: Outperforms communication-centric baselines in success rate and task efficiency across C-WAH and TDW-MAT benchmarks with comparable token usage on three LLM backbones.

problem: Finding an efficient algorithm for solving the 0-1 loss linear classification problem exactly remains open, as the general problem is NP-hard for non-linearly-separable data.
approach: Incremental Cell Enumeration (ICE) algorithm rigorously analyzes combinatorial hyperplane-data point relations to construct an exact solution in O(N^(D+1)) time.
contribution: First standalone algorithm with proven guarantees for exact 0-1 loss linear classification, generalizing to polynomial hypersurface classification in O(N^(G+1)) time.

problem: Large reasoning models suffer from overthinking by generating unnecessarily long reasoning even for simple questions, increasing computational cost and latency.
approach: Decoupled Reward Policy Optimization (DRPO) decouples length-based learning signals for correct versus incorrect rollouts, normalizing rewards for correct samples within positive group only.
contribution: Achieves superior conciseness and reasoning quality compared to GRPO on mathematical reasoning tasks by preventing length penalties from discouraging valid reasoning paths.

problem: Deploying LLMs remains computationally expensive, and existing early exit methods either introduce training overhead or lead to performance degradation through heuristic layer selection.
approach: RAEE models early exit as a distribution prediction problem, leveraging retrieved exit information from similar data to guide backbone model exits without training classifiers.
contribution: Enables zero-shot acceleration across eight downstream tasks while enhancing model performance through corrective exit information from intermediate layers.

problem: Image-to-video diffusion models for generative inbetweening suffer from temporal discontinuities and visual artifacts due to misalignment between forward and backward denoising paths.
approach: Motion Prior Distillation (MPD) suppresses bidirectional mismatch by distilling motion residual from forward path into backward path, avoiding denoising end-conditioned path.
contribution: Yields more temporally coherent inbetweening results with forward motion prior, validated through quantitative evaluation and extensive user studies on practical scenarios.

problem: Existing benchmarks primarily measure correctness, overlooking that true innovation depends on methodological originality and the diversity of approaches behind solutions.
approach: InnoGym introduces performance gain (improvement over best-known solutions) and novelty (methodological differences) metrics on 18 curated real-world engineering and scientific tasks.
contribution: Framework and unified execution environment (iGym) reveal gap between creativity and effectiveness: agents produce novel approaches but lack robustness for consistent performance gains.

problem: Unified multimodal models exhibit modal aphasia: they accurately memorize visual concepts but fail to articulate them textually despite simultaneous training on images and text.
approach: Systematic study through controlled experiments on synthetic datasets and with iconic artwork demonstrates modal aphasia as fundamental property of unified multimodal architectures.
contribution: Reveals widespread vulnerability where models can generate unsafe images despite text-only alignment, highlighting misaligned modality-specific safeguards in multimodal models.

problem: Autoregressive image generation is challenged by bidirectional dependencies in conventional image tokenizations misaligned with unidirectional autoregressive model nature.
approach: AliTok (Aligned Tokenizer) employs bidirectional encoder constrained by causal decoder to produce token sequence with semantic richness and forward-dependency, with prefix tokens and two-stage training.
contribution: 177M model achieves gFID 1.44 and IS 319.5 on ImageNet-256, scaling to 662M reaches gFID 1.28 surpassing SOTA diffusion at 10x faster sampling.

problem: Connecting single-view 2D images with multi-view 3D data remains challenging, and region prompting requires exhaustive multi-frame labeling for spatial understanding.
approach: Spatial Region 3D (SR-3D) vision-language model enriches 2D features with 3D positional embeddings, enabling flexible region prompting via bounding boxes, segmentation masks, or direct 3D annotation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on 2D vision-language and 3D spatial benchmarks while generalizing to in-the-wild videos without sensory 3D inputs or ground-truth annotations.

problem: Decision-focused learning (DFL) struggles in high-dimensional and risk-sensitive settings due to reliance on fixed uncertainty sets, limiting real-world applicability.
approach: Decision-Focused Generative Learning (Gen-DFL) leverages generative models to adaptively model uncertainty and sample from tail regions of learned distribution for worst-case robustness.
contribution: Theoretically achieves improved worst-case performance bounds compared to traditional DFL, empirically outperforms existing methods on various scheduling and logistics optimization problems.

problem: KV caches are typically used only for speed but encode reusable contextual information that could serve other tasks without extra computation.
approach: Treats KV cache as lightweight representation for two applications: Chain-of-Embedding for competitive performance and Fast/Slow Thinking Switching for adaptive reasoning without full hidden states.
contribution: KV-derived representations achieve competitive or superior performance on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2-7B-Instruct, enabling up to 5.7x token reduction with minimal accuracy loss.

problem: Unsupervised disentangled representation learning requires identifiability guarantees but existing methods impose heuristic inductive biases lacking theoretical justification.
approach: Bayesian nonparametric framework with hierarchical mixture prior embeds inductive biases within provably identifiable structure, using nested variational inference for tractable computation.
contribution: Addresses both identifiability guarantees and representation capacity trade-off through nonparametric formulation enabling sufficient latent capacity without violating structural constraints.

problem: Pre-Norm MLLMs suffer from severe norm disparity between high-norm visual tokens and low-norm text tokens, causing asymmetric update dynamics and impaired cross-modal fusion.
approach: Inserts a single LayerNorm layer after visual projector to enforce norm alignment, eliminating representational inertia of visual tokens and enabling symmetric feature fusion.
contribution: Yields significant performance gains on multimodal benchmarks and text-only evaluations like MMLU, demonstrating architectural imbalance resolution improves holistic model capability.

problem: Conducting strong iterative adversarial attacks under limited computational budget is challenging as reducing iterations substantially weakens attack effectiveness.
approach: Proposes fine-grained control mechanism selectively recomputing layer activations at both iteration-wise and layer-wise levels to maximize attack efficacy within fixed budget.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines at equal cost and achieves comparable adversarial training performance with only 30% of original budget.

problem: Extension of rectified flow to infinite-dimensional spaces for functional data generation remains unexplored, limiting applicability to functional generative modeling.
approach: Establishes rigorous functional formulation of rectified flow in infinite-dimensional Hilbert space using superposition principle for continuity equations, extending to functional flow matching.
contribution: Removes restrictive measure-theoretic assumptions in existing functional flow matching theory and demonstrates superior performance compared to existing functional generative models.
